run.question: In the elasticsearch index 'app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }` query and tell me how many hits come back. If that returns zero, find the right field for log level and re-run the query.

report.summary: In index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d the requested term query on the field level for value ERROR returned 0 hits. The index mapping exposes no level field at all; the log-level field present is severity (keyword). Re-running the same term query against severity returned 10 hits. Both searches were time-filtered by the tool on @timestamp to the default 1-hour slice 2026-11-21T05:45:55Z to 2026-11-21T06:45:55Z, while the index reports 30 documents in total.

claims.text: The term query {"term": {"level": "ERROR"}} against index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d returned total value 0 (relation eq), with 0 shard failures, 0 skipped shards and timed_out false.

The mapping of index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d defines exactly four properties: @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword); no level field is mapped, which accounts for the zero hits on the level query.

Re-running the query against severity, {"term": {"severity": "ERROR"}}, returned total value 10 (relation eq); the by_severity terms aggregation on severity returned a single bucket key=ERROR with doc_count 10 and sum_other_doc_count 0, so the matched documents all carry severity ERROR.
Index app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d is green and open with docs.count 30, and the source time range of the documents matched by the severity=ERROR query is 2026-11-21T06:42:01Z to 2026-11-21T06:42:10Z.

gaps: Both searches were constrained by the tool to @timestamp between 2026-11-21T05:45:55Z and 2026-11-21T06:45:55Z (a 1-hour slice), not the full authorized 24-hour window 2026-11-20T06:45:55Z to 2026-11-21T06:45:55Z; ERROR counts outside that hour were not measured and are unknown.

The name and document contents of the searched index could not be cited as a target_ref because only the target identity m0-otel-20260909 was delivered as an allowed target reference; the index-level observations rest on the cited views' query fields.
The level query returned zero hits and the mapping shows no level field, but no check was made for a level field on any other index or alias; only app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d was examined.
Severity values other than ERROR were not enumerated, because the terms aggregation was run with the severity=ERROR term filter applied; a full severity value set for the index remains unknown.
The message and service contents of the 10 ERROR documents were not read, so which service emitted them and what the error text says is unknown.
The index listing and mapping views carry no time range of their own and reflect post-window state; they cannot establish index or field state during the incident window.
next_steps: If per-service attribution is needed, aggregate the severity=ERROR documents in app-275-logs-qe7p2k4d by the service field and read a sample of the message field.
If a longer error history is required, re-run the severity term query over the full authorized 24-hour window in short slices to stay within result-size limits.
